Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

threat noun

also threats, menace, make threats, empty threats

classical

Cic. de Or. 1.247: nōn minīs et vī ac metū (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Quinct. 47: minās jactāre

minae, minārum f. pl.

noun, first declension, plural only · Declension on Wiktionary

threats

Plural even of a single threat. Minās jactāre, to throw threats about (Cic. Quinct. 47). Properly the jutting battlements of a wall (Verg. A. 4.88).

Other words

  • minātiō, minātiōnis f. — a threatening, a threat

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Plaut. Capt. 4.2.19 (Lewis & Short); Cic. de Or. 2.288 · Declension on Wiktionary

    The act of threatening; rare but classical (Plautus, Cicero).

  • perīculum, perīculī n. — a threat in the sense of a danger

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Declension on Wiktionary

    For a threat that is a danger rather than words (“a threat to his health”), Latin speaks of danger: see risk.

Examples

  • quae illaec est minātiō?

    what’s that threat supposed to mean?Plaut. Capt. 4.2.19 (Lewis & Short)

  • Minās tuās nōn timeō.

    I’m not afraid of your threats.composed

See also threaten, threaten, risk, warn.

SourcesLewis & Short: minae · Lewis & Short: minatio · Lewis & Short: periculum
